claims.text: A physics-informed neural network can improve thermal-conductivity prediction accuracy for bulk HfNbTaTiZr relative to existing analytical approaches.
A physics-informed neural network can improve electrical-conductivity prediction accuracy for bulk HfNbTaTiZr relative to existing analytical approaches.
The predicted accuracy advantage is especially pronounced when defects or oxygen impurities are present.
PINNs use deep learning to solve nonlinear partial differential equations.
The proposed model is applicable to bulk HfNbTaTiZr both without added oxygen and with 1 wt.% oxygen.
Defects and oxygen impurities mediate the proposed improvement in predictive accuracy.
PINNs can incorporate physical laws and constraints into their neural-network architecture.
Incorporating physical laws and constraints enables more accurate modeling of complex physical problems.
Existing analytical conductivity approaches have limited accuracy for this alloy.
Existing analytical approaches are restricted to perfect, defect-free crystals.
The proposed prediction domain includes temperatures from 0 to 200 K.
The proposed prediction domain includes temperatures from 300 to 1200 K.
Model performance is limited by the quality and quantity of training data.
Model performance is limited by the selected PINN architecture and hyperparameters.
Thermal conductivity at 500 K for the specimen containing 1 wt.% oxygen is the proposed experimental benchmark.
Failure to predict the 500 K thermal conductivity within ±5% of experiment would falsify the stated effectiveness criterion.
